methodology: Solved this session by extracting the calculator's own Angular "sellerNetForm" component logic from its lazy-loaded route chunk (webpack chunk 7, hash 8a01902021d264bdb338 -- fetched by replaying the runtime bundle's own chunk-hash map, since this route is not referenced in the shell page's main.js until a user actually clicks into the seller-net-sheet flow). This resolved the 2026-08-07 session's blocker: `POST /api/rates/fees/estimatefeesforsellernet` was 500ing with unhelpful ProblemDetails errors because the guessed flat `PropertyState`/`PropertyCounty`/`PropertyCity` fields (borrowed from the sibling, differently-shaped `sellernet/calculate` endpoint's own validation-error field names) do not match this endpoint's real schema. The component's own `prepareCalculateFeeRequest()` method reveals the actual required body: `Properties: [{City, County, IsPrimary: true, State}]` (nested, not flat), `Loans: [{LienPosition: 0, LoanAmount}]`, `TransactionProductType: {ProductTypeId: 0, TransactionTypeId: 0}` (0/0 confirmed correct for this flow, not a placeholder), `calculateTaxRequest: {}` (an empty class instance), `SettlementStatementVersion: "CD"`, and empty arrays/objects for `premiumDiscounts`/`Endorsements`/`PriorLenderPolicy`/`PriorOwnerPolicy`. Confirmed via `GET /api/rates/State/GetCalculationEnabledStates` (also public, no auth) that this one API has `isCalculationEnabled: true` for 47 states + DC -- a single new, genuinely distinct 5th major-underwriter source (WFG National Title, a separate corporate family from FNF/Old Republic/Stewart/First American, all already on file elsewhere in this survey) usable across nearly every remaining below-threshold scarce state in one technique. No personal-data field (name/email/phone) exists anywhere in this request shape. Separately confirmed via static inspection of the same chunk's hardcoded `feesConfiguration` sort-weight table that WFG has only itemized its settlement/closing HUD-fee line items for 7 states (WA, CA, TX, OR, AZ, NV, CO) -- for every other state (including this one) the tool returns a premium-only result (Owner's Title Insurance Premium, no settlement/search/doc-prep breakdown), which per this project's 2026-08-05 FNF scoping correction is still valid, dated calculator-harvest evidence.

provider: Fidelity National Title Insurance Company — FNF National Rate Calculator (ratecalculator.fnf.com)
scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan amount, Greenville County (SC's most-populous county), residential resale, Fidelity National Title underwriter selected.
methodology: Solves the 2026-08-06 session's logged 'unsolved AmountLoan1 postback quirk' for SC (and separately UT, see UT.json) -- the quirk was never a real server-side block, it was a bug in that session's own replay script: every extracted hidden-field dict included the page's <input type="submit"> button name=value pairs (e.g. btnGeneralNext="Next") carried forward unchanged into later POSTs, causing the server to treat every subsequent postback as an implicit re-click of that button and silently fast-forward/desync the wizard state (masquerading as a 'silently dropped AmountLoan1 value'). Fixed by excluding submit/button/image/reset <input> types from the carried-forward field set and only including a given button's name=value on the specific POST that is actually 'clicking' it. SC's one extra required question ("Does this transaction qualify under CFPB's TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule?", CFPB_IsQualified) already defaults to 'Yes' (value=1) with no cascade, unlike UT's 3-question CPL-eligibility chain. Recipe: GET with ?ID=FNF&state=SC, POST ddlCounty='greenville' (own __EVENTTARGET), POST ddlUnderwriters='fnt' (own __EVENTTARGET, Fidelity National Title), POST btnGeneralNext='Next' to reach the Amounts panel, POST TranType$ddl='PropertyPurchase' (own __EVENTTARGET), POST AmountPurchase$txt='$500,000.00' (own __EVENTTARGET), POST AmountLoan1$txt='$400,000.00' (own __EVENTTARGET) -- now echoed correctly, POST btnFinish='Finish' (CFPB_IsQualified's default 'Yes' carried through) for the final quote. No personal-data fields required at any step.

methodology: This is Old Republic's *second* calculator tool (distinct from `ortconline.com/Web2`, whose own footprint does not include SC/LA/MS -- see CALCULATORS.md's state-coverage note). Prior sessions (2026-07-29, 2026-08-01) found `Location=SC` hard-rejected by this tool's NoBot anti-bot control ("You are not authorized to access the site. Code: 2") even with a realistic Referer/User-Agent -- logged as blocked. This session retried it (per the standing blocked-source-retry protocol, and because the 2026-08-08 NM harvest already found the same NoBot block had loosened for at least one other state) and it now works cleanly: GET `EmbedRateCalc.aspx?Location=SC&cms=https://www.oldrepublictitle.com/` 302-redirects through a session-establishing URL (`/(S(...))/RateCalc.aspx?...`) to a real form, no login/credentials needed. Confirms the 2026-08-08 NM finding that this NoBot block is intermittent/agent-or-session-reputation-based, not a permanent state-level block -- worth retrying for any state still logged NoBot-blocked. Recipe once past the redirect: POST `ddlPolicyCategory=5` (SIMULTANEOUS LOAN & OWNERS, own __EVENTTARGET) to reveal the Owner's/Loan policy-type dropdowns and liability-amount fields; POST `ddlPolicyType1=11528` (OWNERS - BASIC, own __EVENTTARGET); POST `ddlPolicyType2=11535` (SIMUL LOAN, own __EVENTTARGET); POST `txtLiabilityAmt=500000` (Purchase Price, own __EVENTTARGET); POST `txtCrLiabilityAmt=400000` (Loan Amount, own __EVENTTARGET); POST `btnCalculate=Calculate` for the final quote, rendered inline as an HTML results table (`gvwResults`). methodology: Harvested via Stewart's discoverable `/api/SRC/*` JSON REST API (stewartratecalculator.com), driven entirely by plain HTTP GET/POST (Python requests.Session(), cookie jar) with no browser/JS execution and no personal-data fields, replaying the full recipe documented in this project's CALCULATORS.md (2026-08-14 'SOLVED' entry): GET the LoanEstimate/Netsheet page to scrape a fresh antiforgery cookie + __RequestVerificationToken; GET /api/SRC/propertysearch to resolve the county FIPS code and a default zip; GET /api/SRC/providers to find the county's real settlement office(s) (used to set ProviderID on the QuoteType=3 flow so the itemized settlement-fee list is populated -- an empty ProviderID silently returns a null itemized list); GET /api/SRC/statesettings and /api/SRC/ernstlookup for state-level defaults; build the QuoteRequestRoot JSON by hand (Owner's Policy $500,000 / Lender's Policy $400,000, BASIC coverage, standard Sale/Purchase with Mortgage transaction); POST /api/SRC/quote twice -- QuoteType=2 (Netsheet, pageBuyerSeller=seller) for Recording/CFPB2015 transfer-tax figures, and QuoteType=3 (LoanEstimate, pageBuyerSeller=buyer, IsCalculatePremium=True, IsCalculateTitleServiceFee=True) for the itemized Pricing.TitleServiceFee.ItemizedTitleServiceFeeList settlement-fee line items. One new gotcha found and fixed this session: stewartratecalculator.com's bare apex domain 301-redirects every POST to the www subdomain, and that redirect's response body hangs indefinitely on this sandbox's proxied connection (a 30s+ read timeout with 0 bytes received) -- fixed by targeting https://www.stewartratecalculator.com directly, skipping the apex redirect entirely; this is an environment/proxy artifact, not a sign the endpoint is blocked. Also confirmed the documented /api/SRC/providers gotcha firsthand: for a single-provider county the response's `Provider` field is a bare object, not a one-element list -- must be normalized before indexing or ProviderID silently stays empty and every itemized-fee list comes back null (looks exactly like a genuine empty result).
